Nippybot raises angel funding for UK delivery-robot deployments

The Middlesbrough startup plans more robots and site deployments spanning hospitals, campuses and other controlled environments.

RoboticsTomorrow ↗5 November 2026English editorial summary
Story

Funding deployment work

Nippybot disclosed an angel investment round of undisclosed size in a November 5 announcement. Based in Middlesbrough in the Tees Valley, it develops robots for short-distance transport of food, parcels and other goods. Funding supports additional robot production, technology development and commercial partnerships.

Targeting repetitive goods movement

The company is exploring logistics facilities, hospitals, universities, business parks and other controlled sites. Its stated objective is reliable everyday delivery, beyond simply demonstrating movement between two points. Opportunities are being explored across these sectors rather than presented as completed nationwide deployment.

Human oversight remains available

Autonomous navigation is paired with remote operational capabilities so people can supervise when necessary. Founder Samson Adewole says additional sites will provide operational data and new problems to solve. The announcement does not disclose a production quantity, newly contracted customer names or measured delivery-success rates.
